slides.3.title: 🌡️ Climate and Terroir
slides.3.content:
🌤️ Continental Climate

Summer: Hot and dry (25–30°C)

Winter: Cold with snow (0–5°C)

Autumn: Frequent fog (Nebbia)

Diurnal variation: Large (10–15°C)

🌫️ The Origin of Nebbiolo's Name

At harvest time in autumn, the hills of Piemonte are often shrouded in thick fog (Nebbia) — giving Nebbiolo its name.

The fog slows ripening, allowing the grapes to accumulate richer flavours and tannins.

slides.6.title: ⚪ White Wines and Sparkling Wines
slides.6.content:
🥂 Gavi DOCG

Grape: Cortese

Style: Fresh, mineral, lemon, green apple

Acidity: High

Food pairing: Seafood, white meat, salads, Vitello Tonnato

Drinking window: 1–5 years

🍾 Moscato d'Asti DOCG

Grape: Moscato Bianco

Style: Off-dry sparkling, peach, lychee, rose

Alcohol: Low (5–6.5%)

Food pairing: Desserts, fruit, brunch

Character: Fresh, low-pressure bubble (Frizzante)

🎉 Asti DOCG

Grape: Moscato Bianco

Style: Sweet sparkling, floral

Alcohol: 6–9%

Food pairing: Cake, Panettone, celebrations

Character: Full sparkling (Spumante)

slides.8.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
slides.8.questions.0.question: What is 'Nebbia' in Piemonte, and how does it relate to wine?
slides.8.questions.0.options.1: B. The autumn fog that gave Nebbiolo its name
slides.8.questions.0.options.2: C. A special type of soil
slides.8.questions.0.options.3: D. A cold wind from the Alps
slides.8.questions.0.explanation: Nebbia means 'fog'. It is a defining autumn climate feature of Piemonte. Nebbiolo grape takes its name directly from Nebbia — the fog helps slow ripening, adding complexity and concentration.
slides.8.questions.1.question: What do Barolo and Barbaresco have in common? (Multiple choice)
slides.8.questions.1.options.0: A. Both are made from Nebbiolo
slides.8.questions.1.explanation: Barolo and Barbaresco are both top-tier DOCG red wines made from 100% Nebbiolo, produced in Piemonte. Both are dry wines, not sweet.
slides.8.questions.2.question: What is the key stylistic difference between Barolo and Barbaresco?
slides.8.questions.2.options.0: A. Barolo uses white grapes; Barbaresco uses red
slides.8.questions.2.options.1: B. Barolo is powerful and needs long ageing; Barbaresco is elegant and more approachable
slides.8.questions.2.options.2: C. Barbaresco has much higher alcohol than Barolo
slides.8.questions.2.explanation: Barolo is called the 'King of Wines' — powerful and structured, requiring at least 3 years' ageing. Barbaresco is the 'Queen' — more elegant and refined, needing at least 2 years and approachable earlier.
slides.8.questions.3.question: What are the defining characteristics of Moscato d'Asti DOCG?
slides.8.questions.3.options.1: B. Off-dry, low-alcohol, lightly sparkling white wine (~5.5% ABV)
slides.8.questions.3.options.2: C. Fully fermented, bone-dry white wine
slides.8.questions.3.explanation: Moscato d'Asti is a Frizzante (lightly sparkling) sweet white wine made from Moscato Bianco, with about 5% alcohol, and aromas of peach, apricot, and honey — perfect with desserts.
slides.8.questions.4.question: Which of the following are core red grape varieties of Piemonte? (Multiple choice)
slides.8.questions.4.explanation: Nebbiolo (the king), Barbera (high-acid everyday red), and Dolcetto (easy-drinking) are Piemonte's three core red varieties. Sangiovese is mainly grown in Tuscany and rarely found in Piemonte.

slides.10.title: 🎓 Key Takeaways
slides.10.points.0: ✓ Piemonte is Italy's highest-quality wine region
slides.10.points.1: ✓ Nebbiolo is 'Italy's King', producing Barolo and Barbaresco
slides.10.points.3: ✓ Barbera: high acidity, low tannins — excellent value
slides.10.points.4: ✓ Moscato d'Asti: the world's most famous off-dry sparkling wine
quiz.0.question: What is Piemonte's most famous red grape variety?
quiz.0.explanation: Nebbiolo is Piemonte's most celebrated variety, used to make top wines such as Barolo and Barbaresco.
quiz.1.question: Which wine is known as the 'King of Wines'?
quiz.1.explanation: Barolo is celebrated as the 'King of Wines' (Re dei Vini) and is one of Italy's greatest red wines.
quiz.2.question: What is the key stylistic contrast between Barolo and Barbaresco?
quiz.2.options.0: Barolo is elegant; Barbaresco is powerful
quiz.2.options.1: Barolo is powerful; Barbaresco is elegant
quiz.2.explanation: Barolo is the 'King' (powerful, firm tannins); Barbaresco is the 'Queen' (refined, silky). Both are exceptional but distinctly different in style.
quiz.3.question: What is Barbera's defining profile?
quiz.3.explanation: Barbera's distinctiveness lies in its low tannins combined with high acidity, making it highly food-friendly and approachable for everyday drinking.
